article.title: “Paraguay Is in Dire Need of Change”: Senator on Bank Collapse & Political Crisis
article.content: The collapse of Ueno Bank in Paraguay has plunged the country into crisis and led to the ouster of right-wing President Santiago Peña, a staunch ally of the Trump administration. At least 3 million people — nearly half of Paraguay’s population — lost access to their accounts on November 3 after regulators seized the insolvent bank amid allegations of widespread fraud. Peña, who had close ties to Ueno and appointed a former executive to lead Paraguay’s central bank, attempted to resign the presidency following the bank’s collapse. Lawmakers, however, rejected his resignation and impeached him instead, thereby stripping him of immunity from prosecution. He has since been placed under house arrest. For more on the bank collapse and its aftermath, Democracy Now! spoke with left-wing Senator Esperanza Martínez, who called for a broad “national pact” among various political parties to navigate the crisis and institute reforms. “Paraguay is in dire need of change,” she said.
